structure_rules: Organize by component and responsibility, not by implementation language. app/ has cmd/, internal/ and frontend/ directly; never reintroduce app/go/.
Commands compose concrete owners. Service contracts live with their owner; implementations live under that owner’s internal/.
A directory is a Go package. Extract a real responsibility and its concrete API before moving receiver methods; keep tests beside the behavior they verify.
Shared capability packages stay shared when there are real cross-service consumers. Avoid a generic common package, transitional shims or interfaces invented only for a move.

remaining_work.title: Separate runtime lifecycle coordination
remaining_work.target_status: candidate name; not an approved file allocation
remaining_work.summary: A concrete lifecycle owner would hold admission generations, transition serialization, cancellation, drain and worker joins. Coordinator would compose it with bootstrap, Session, Execution and ingress owners. Existing internal/lifecycle remains the resource/contract leaf.
how: Map every shared Runtime field and lock to the admission, transition and close operations that use it; resolve shutdown/reconciliation ownership first.
Simplify one bounded lifecycle path under existing race tests. Choose a concrete owner API only after late callbacks, generation fences, cancellation and worker joins have an explicit contract.

Then extract the relevant types and methods into runcontrol, moving tests with behavior and updating command/BUILD/docs callers in one PR. The listed files are source locations to split, not wholesale rename instructions.
remaining_work.gate: Do not move Runtime receiver methods while they still require mutable access to the coordinator aggregate. Exact type and file allocation is undecided.
remaining_work.preserve: Admission generations; execution/session fencing; journal sealing; final History ACK; ordered cancel/drain/join. No replay and no extra test hooks.

remaining_work.title: Separate GitHub state query responsibilities
remaining_work.target_status: candidate name; not an approved file allocation
remaining_work.summary: A private GitHub-state helper could own refresh/access/subject query details. Store must remain the transaction authority for shared provider observations, inbox updates, receipts and notifications. Ingest/delivery writes that cross those facts stay with Store.
how: Trace which GitHubState operations share Store transactions with inbox and subscription writes. Specify the typed transaction/fence inputs and lock order before moving code.
Keep transaction begin/commit, the GitHub ingress advisory lock, row locks and commit-time NOTIFY under one authority; never create independent commits per query family.
After that contract is checked, extract the query/type responsibility into store/internal/githubstate with owner-local tests. Update every consumer and Bazel target together.
remaining_work.gate: No filename-prefix split or new public Store forwarding API. Exact methods and types that can cross the transaction boundary remain to be decided.
remaining_work.preserve: GitHub advisory lock before inbox locks; lease and installation generations; receipt/cursor atomicity; NOTIFY on commit.

remaining_work.title: Choose privileged peer authentication
remaining_work.kind: contract design; no filesystem move selected
remaining_work.summary: Keep the current shared peer TLS owner at net/peertls. Later compare Kubernetes-independent service SPIFFE, audience-scoped ServiceAccount/TokenReview over pinned TLS, and explicit per-target configuration. No mechanism is selected.
how: Inventory callers, peer identity and delegated authority separately.
Design the mechanism and migration/configuration surface; then choose any additional owner boundaries from that contract.
remaining_work.gate: Deferred by the operator. Do not move peer TLS under identity/transport or infer an authentication decision from a path change.
remaining_work.preserve: Role and delegation boundaries; peer URI/EKU checks, rotation and expiry closure.

remaining_work.title: Align protobuf namespaces with filesystem ownership
remaining_work.kind: declaration and wire-contract migration; no filesystem move selected
remaining_work.summary: Align package and go_package declarations with the directories that own the contracts. Existing source owners remain the starting point; generated APIs and wire names need an explicit compatibility plan.
how: Inventory every .proto package, go_package, generated import path, service/method full name and persisted Any/type URL.
Choose the canonical namespace per owner. Plan compatibility for stored payloads and clients before changing declarations or generated labels.
Migrate contracts and all Go/Python/TypeScript consumers together in contract-scoped PRs; ordinary package moves do not rename wire protocols.
remaining_work.gate: Naming is deferred until the wire-name and stored-payload migration is specified. The goal tree does not invent proto moves.
remaining_work.preserve: RPC full names, Any type URLs, stored payload readability and generated client compatibility until explicitly migrated.

remaining_work_note: All previously dispatched ownership groups have merged and are removed from this plan. No ready filesystem move is asserted by this refresh; two candidate extractions require ownership contracts, and authentication/protobuf design remains deferred.
